records.proposition: Ascorbate added to the tested inhibitor-containing meal increases non-haem iron absorption; this is an upstream supply proposition, not a dopamine outcome.

rationale.D: The abstract measures the exact upstream absorption endpoint.
rationale.B: Original allocation, controls and exclusions remain unretrieved.
rationale.P: Original paired uncertainty and complete subgroup data remain unretrieved.
rationale.R: Independent primary studies identified, but exact-proposition appraisal remains unfinished.

limitations: No brain iron, dopamine or clinical endpoint measured.
Do not substitute a review or citation count for primary appraisal.

records.proposition: Verified phytase dephytinisation increased iron absorption from the tested water-reconstituted cereal porridges, with material-specific exceptions.

rationale.D: The measured isotope endpoint matches the bounded absorption proposition.
rationale.B: Within-participant labelled comparisons and measured phytate; sequential meal order and unreported masking leave residual concerns.
rationale.P: Reported paired ratios support direction; small cohorts and material-dependent magnitudes prevent a precise transferable effect.
rationale.R: Separate study cohorts within the same research programme provide partial confirmation; not independent-team replication.

limitations: No generic household soaking claim.
Milk matrices and high-tannin sorghum did not consistently respond.
No dopamine outcome.

records.proposition: Five days of 30%-energy-restricted low-fat feeding was associated with lower striatal D2/D3 PET binding potential than eucaloric baseline in adults with obesity.

rationale.D: Exact population, protocol and imaging endpoint are assessed, not dopamine release or benefit.
rationale.B: Randomised diet order, supervised intake and imaging sensitivity checks; baseline always precedes restriction and incomplete scans leave residual concerns.
rationale.P: Corrected clusters and completer checks support a bounded observation; small sample and localisation uncertainty limit magnitude/generalisation.
rationale.R: One verified dietary PET dataset; the separate VLCD study is not replication of this precise exposure and striatal proposition.

limitations: No significant PET difference between reduced-fat and reduced-carbohydrate diets.
The separately measured food-cue fMRI comparison differs; do not merge endpoints.
Binding does not identify receptor change versus dopamine occupancy.
No therapeutic advantage established.

records.proposition: The tested approximately ten-day very-low-calorie protocol causes lower substantia-nigra D2/D3 binding potential in women with obesity.

rationale.D: The exact protocol and SN imaging endpoint were measured.
rationale.B: For a causal intervention claim, the uncontrolled before/after design leaves time, retest and concurrent changes inseparable from the diet; this is a verified critical design limitation, not missing retrieval.
rationale.P: SN changed from 2.69 to 2.59, paired t(14)=3.24, p=.006; small sample and uncertain magnitude prevent high precision.
rationale.R: One verified dataset; bariatric surgery and different dietary protocols are not exact replications.

limitations: Observed change is not proof of causality or improved signalling.
Other regional changes were nonsignificant trends.
Leptin association does not establish mediation.
Admission requires adjudication if presented as a recommended optimisation rather than bounded research observation.

records.proposition: In the tested porridge/black-tea protocol, iron absorption was higher when tea was consumed one hour after rather than with the meal.

rationale.D: Exact upstream isotope absorption comparison; no dopamine inference.
rationale.B: Same-participant standardised meals and objective isotope measurements, but fixed nonrandomised sequence leaves period effects unresolved.
rationale.P: Paired difference 2.2 percentage points, p=.046; 12 women and broad dispersion limit transferable effect size.
rationale.R: One verified exact timing dataset; thesis, conference and journal versions are the same study.

limitations: Not green tea, optimal timing, long-term iron status or brain delivery.
Population restricted to iron-replete women.

records.proposition: During the tested 40-minute supine cycling protocol, striatal raclopride binding was lower than at rest in healthy young men.

rationale.D: Exact exercise and PET endpoint are assessed, without inferring causal cognitive mediation.
rationale.B: Randomised condition order and matched timing; exploratory PET analysis, exclusions and possible reference-region blood-flow effects remain.
rationale.P: PET condition effect p=.050 in 16 men; small sample and wide correlation intervals constrain confidence in magnitude.
rationale.R: One exact during-exercise PET experiment. Earlier post-treadmill PET was null with different timing; EMS experiments do not replicate dopamine measurement.

limitations: No sustained benefit or general exercise prescription.
Reaction-time correlation is not mediation.
Left-putamen correlation and task-accuracy outcomes were not significant.

records.proposition: One night of total sleep deprivation was associated with lower ventral-striatal D2/D3 availability than rested sleep in the tested healthy men.

rationale.D: Exact acute sleep comparison and PET endpoint.
rationale.B: Randomised session order and observed sleep conditions; unrecorded wakefulness prompts and mental-state effects remain.
rationale.P: Small sample and region-dependent findings; reported binding difference supports direction but not a precise habitual-sleep prescription.
rationale.R: Related 2008 study recovered, but cohort overlap/independence requires verification before a replication factor is finalised.

limitations: Receptor downregulation is an interpretation, not uniquely measured mechanism.
No recommended sleep-duration trial.
